item.title: DeepSeek Super Agent：真正值得看的，是「一切皆插件」的 Harness
item.author: AI news / DeepSeek Super Agent explainer
item.description:
同模型换九套编码 Agent，成本能差出一个数量级。Instacart 和 Box 的 CTO 都把票投给了 harness。

乔木改写

很多人把 DeepSeek 新开源的东西叫「Claude Code 的回答」。视频作者觉得，更值得盯的是它怎么被做出来的。

Super Agent 不是又一个聊天窗口。它听团队已经在用的地方：GitHub Issue / PR，以及飞书。有权限的人提需求后，它开 work item，在独立目录里干活，再带着 PR 回来。DeepSeek 自己说，这是研究原型，很多工程甚至是编码 Agent 写的。

底座是八月发布的 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）。口号很绝：一切皆插件。路由、工具注册、会话日志，连 Agent loop 本身都是插件，底下是叫 Cordis 的组合框架。两个关键能力：

  • 时间可组合：卸掉一个组件，它做过的注册会完整回滚
  • 空间可组合：组件声明依赖，运行时按依赖上下线

Frontier Harness Eval 用同一模型 Kimi K3、同一批 30 个任务，跑九套 harness。Codex 通过率 66.7%，DeepSeek creator 模式和 Claude Code 都是 63.3%，但单次成功任务成本大约 $3.28 vs $18.34。样本不大，方向很清楚：换 harness，成败和账单都会变。

Super Agent 的架构也很有意思：上层一个长驻 router 负责人和分发，下层 worker 各自隔离会话。外部触发先过确定性门禁（在不在白名单、有没有真正 @ Agent），过了才进模型。Worker 认领 ticket 后直接订阅那条对话，评论不再绕 router，他们测过，关掉这层后 router 决策量大约多 30%。压力测试里触发从每分钟 1 次拉到 40 次，批量处理后单次决策时间反而下降。结论有点反直觉：router 往往更适合轻模型，重模型留给 worker。

作者访谈过 Instacart 和 Box 的 CTO，两边都认为现阶段 harness 比模型更重要。视频收尾也留了清醒提醒：这是原型，安全问题（提示注入、凭据泄漏、跨设备权限）他们自己也承认没完全解决。

如果你只记住一句：别再只评模型。同一模型至少丢进两三个 harness 再下判断，不然你骂的可能是壳，不是芯。

原文

DeepSeek Super Agent and why the harness matters

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OrcsMi2-IcM

DeepSeek Super Agent and why the harness matters

Source: YouTube https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OrcsMi2-IcM

Okay, so this past weekend, DeepSeek released something that a lot of people out there are calling the answer to Claude Code. It's an agent that sits on a GitHub repo. It watches the issues and pull requests, and when someone on your team asks it to do something, It then goes off into its own session, does the work, and comes back with a PR Now, while that's cool in itself, that's not really the part that I want to talk about here. The part that I find really interesting is how they built it. The whole thing is just a set of plugins dropped into their agent harness.

When the DeepSeek Harness came out back in August, the plugin architecture is really cool. The new thing DeepSeek launched is called Super Agent. Along with the repo, they've written an article on X called Exploring Super Agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System. They're upfront that this is a research prototype, not an official DeepSeek product. Ideas and engineering were often written by coding agents themselves.

Basic idea: instead of you opening a session and talking to an agent, the agent listens to where your team already works — GitHub, and Feishu. When someone allowed asks it for something, it opens a work item, spins up its own session, does the work, replies back usually with a PR.

On the VentureBeat podcast Beyond the Pilot, CTOs of Instacart and Box both said the harness matters more than the model right now.

Frontier Harness Eval: same model (Kimi K3) through nine coding agent harnesses. Codex 66.7% pass rate; DeepSeek Harness creator config and Claude Code both 63.3%. DeepSeek ~$3.28 per successful task vs Claude Code ~$18.34. Gap cheapest to most expensive ~17.5x. Harness changes cost, caching, speed, and success rate even with model held constant.

DeepSeek Harness (DSH) MIT licensed, web UI, not locked to DeepSeek models. Tagline: everything is a plugin — router, tool registry, session log, even the agent loop. Built on Cordis (spatiotemporal composability): temporal (unload reverses everything) and spatial (dependencies activate/deactivate).

Modes: standard, PTC, minimal, creator — different plugin sets. Creator: describe a plugin in chat and agent writes/installs it.

Super Agent integrates via cordis.patch: core Super Agent plugin, GitHub watcher, Feishu watcher. Workers: stripped preset, no questions/plan/web fetch/sub-agents; long shell jobs backgrounded. Architecture: long-running router session + isolated worker sessions. Triggers go through a deterministic gate (allow-list) before the model. Tickets carry a mandate. Workers subscribe to conversation so PR comments skip the router (30% fewer router decisions when on).

Under load (1→40 triggers/min), batching made time per decision drop 6.4s→1.6s. Router can use a cheap/fast model; stronger models for workers.

Philosophy: take as little human attention as possible and give as much value as possible.

Caveats: prototype; published code ≠ internal; narrow (GitHub/Feishu); synthetic benchmarks; security (prompt injection, credentials) not fully solved.

Bigger point: harnesses evolving fast via composable plugins without forking the core.

item.title: Sarah Guo：非工程师也想改自己的软件，我之前判断错了
item.author: Sarah Guo
item.description:
从「我好有掌控感」到「没人会给我做这个工作流」，欲望光谱比想象中宽。

乔木改写

Sarah Guo 写得很短，但足以改一条产品假设。

几年前，她不太相信大量非工程师真的想自己做、或改个人软件。现在她认错了。她看到的欲望大概分几档：

  • 我感觉自己很有力量
  • 没人会给我做我要的工作流 / 个性化
  • 能不能让我当几周产品经理，把这个天天烦我的点修掉

事后看几乎是常识：只要「省力 / 能力」比值够好，人就会动手做自己的软件。

这和「人人都该学编程」不是一回事。更接近：当 Agent 把实现成本压下去之后，个人软件会从极客玩具，变成普通人处理生活摩擦的默认选项。

对做工具的人来说，下一步产品问题大概是：你是继续做一个封闭的成品，还是留出足够安全的口子，让用户能把自己的流程焊进去。

原文

Non-engineers do want to make personal software

a few years ago, I started out skeptical that many non-engineers really wanted to make/mod their own personal software -- but I've come around, think I was wrong. range of desires from:

  • I feel so powerful
  • no one will make me the workflow/personalization I need
  • can I just PM the product for a few weeks and fix this thing that is driving me crazy

obvious in retrospect, but if the ease:power ratio is good enough, of course people will make their own software

item.title: Rauch：Vercel 内部那个「惊人有效」的安全 Agent，终于对外开放了
item.author: Guillermo Rauch
item.description:
每行代码自动审计。他的判断很直白：你不能指望工程师记得装技能，或掷骰子赌第一版就安全。

乔木改写

Guillermo Rauch 等这一天很久了。

Vercel 内部有个安全 Agent，昵称叫 @hacker。Rauch 的原话是「astonishingly effective」：每一行代码都会被自动审计。现在，同样的能力对外开放了。打开之后，不管你的项目是不是部署在 Vercel 上，都可以挂到仓库上跑。

他为什么这么急着推？因为边界条件已经变了。

你不能只靠工程师「记得装一个安全技能」，也不能只靠 prompt 里写一句「请写得安全一点」，更不能赌模型第一次就吐出靠谱代码。安全要变成默认流水线，而不是人品考验。

配套产品是 Vercel Security Review（公测）。按官方说明，它挂在每次 GitHub push 上：扫变更、在 PR 留评论、进 Security 面板，也可以让 Vercel Agent 验证并直接提修复。扫描的是 diff，所以通常几秒结束，预览和生产部署都能跑。

Rauch 还特意点了一句：这套东西是安全团队自己做出来的。很多公司正忙着招人补安全编制；如果你想「把一个安全团队下载成软件」，这大概是今天最接近的形态。

我读完更在意的是分工。写代码的 Agent 越来越多，审代码的 Agent 如果不跟上，中间那截空档会变成默认攻击面。Rauch 这篇文章，其实是在说：安全也该产品化，而且要产品到「每 push 必审」。

原文

Vercel internal security agent @hacker now available

I've been looking forward to this day, because Vercel has an internal security agent that is astonishingly effective (lovingly called @𝚑𝚊𝚌𝚔𝚎𝚛). Every single line of code gets audited, automatically.

You can now get the same power. Just enable it on all your repos (this product works whether you host on Vercel or not) and your peace of mind will increase tremendously. You'll see it catch things that every other agent misses.

Why: you cannot just bank on your engineers having a skill installed, prompting "please make secure", or rolling the weights' dice that the code is good out of the gate.

The other cool thing about this is that this was entirely developed by our security team. A lot of companies out there are probably in a mad rush right now trying to staff up. If you wanted to 'download a security team' as software, this is the closest you get today.

item.title: 25 岁做到 5 亿年化收入：Slash 怎么靠「超级小生意」打穿金融
item.author: Victor Cardenas
item.description:
不到 100 人，年化收入过 $500m。Victor 把方法写得很清楚：找 SuperSMB，卖给他们，为他们做产品。

乔木改写

Victor Cardenas 宣布，Slash 年化收入刚越过 $500m。去年大约 $150m，再上一年 $50m。团队不到 100 人。他 25 岁。

长文的核心概念叫 SuperSMB：人很少、收入很高、决策极快的公司。AI 让这类创业者密度暴涨。Victor 给的数据里，平台上 88% 的资产来自 35 岁以下创始人的公司，65% 的月支出流来自近三年成立的公司。

他对销售的判断几乎是反常识的：

以前 B2B 得在「大单但慢」和「小单但快」之间二选一。卖给 SuperSMB，你可以同时要到大金额和短周期。

怎么找到他们？Slash 不用 Clay / ZoomInfo，也不靠冷邮件。三条硬要求：靠产品赢得转介、人必须在场（群、论坛、会议）、第一天就给人而不是把高级支持锁在员工数门槛后面。他说，一个销售一年带进超过 $1 亿收入，在他们团队是真实发生过的。

产品侧同样围绕这群人：全球可用、Agent-ready（仪表盘能做的，API / MCP 也能做）、懂行业工作流、尽量 all-in-one、定价激进。他的原话是，靠砍自己的内部成本赚钱，别靠抬客户价格。

读完最大的感觉是：AI native 创业者已经大到值得单独开一条银行产品线。谁还按「传统 SMB vs 企业」做分组，谁就会把最快的那批客人让出去。

原文

Slash hit 500m annual revenue with 88 people. We invented a new playbook:

Last month, we crossed $500m in annualized gross revenue, up from roughly $150m last year and $50m the year before. Our business is getting larger, and our growth is accelerating. Slash is one of the fastest growing fintech companies of all time, and we have a team of under 100 people.

Our growth can be almost entirely attributed to the fact that we are 100x better at building for and selling to truly AI native entrepreneurs than our competitors. In this article I’m going to talk about three things that helped me build a half a billion dollar revenue business by 25: The rise of the “SuperSMB”, very lean companies with tons of revenue. How to find and sell to the “SuperSMB”. How to build product for the “SuperSMB”. Bookmark this, my promise is that this will be the MOST valuable read of your week.

THE RISE OF THE SUPER-SMB AI is causing a Cambrian explosion of entrepreneurs. In the last three years: U.S. business applications reached roughly 5.6 million in 2025, up about 60% from 3.5 million in 2019. Every 26 seconds, a Shopify store makes its first sale. The median Stripe Atlas startup generated 39% more revenue in its first six months in 2025 than its 2024 counterpart. The “fastest from $0 -> $XXm” isn’t a phenomenon that’s restricted to tech companies. Businesses are growing faster in every sector of the economy. These entrepreneurs are young. Slash customers spend billions of dollars every month, and hold billions of dollars on platform: Over 88% of the assets on the Slash platform belong to businesses with founders under the age of 35. 72% of the spend on Slash is done by businesses with founders under the age of 35. item.title: Levelsio：全站开销砍到约 $300/月，Claude 帮他一年省下近三万刀月费
item.author: Pieter Levels
item.description:
2 万付费用户、2.52 亿访客、2.4PB 流量。AI 最擅长的，可能是帮你找到自己看不见的浪费。

乔木改写

Pieter Levels 又晒了一张成本表。

他所有网站加在一起，服务着大约 2 万付费用户、2.52 亿访客、24 亿请求、2.4PB 带宽。常规业务开销现在只剩大约 $300/月。如果把 Photo AI 的 GPU（约 $7000/月）和 R2（约 $800/月）算进去，大概 $8000/月。

更刺眼的是降幅。他列了 Claude Code 帮他抠出来的账，合计接近 $34,000/月：

  • 视频模型换更便宜的、部分任务走 Google Cloud Credits 和市价转售，GPU 从 $36k 降到 $7k
  • 服务器合并，取消 DigitalOcean / Linode，迁到 Hetzner，约省 $3k
  • Backblaze 无限版本改成 30 天生命周期，备份费从 $1200 降到 $26
  • R2 加生命周期，90 天后进低频，从 $1200 降到 $800
  • Cloudflare 域名清掉不用的，尤其是越来越贵的 .io
  • 连 Claude 自己的 Max 20x 订阅也被降到 $100，因为他根本用不满

连 Photo AI 算上，总成本比去年砍了大约九成，接近他十年前刚创业时的量级。

他自己也说了一句很冷的话：短期看，AI 擅长找成本节约，对经济未必友好；长期看，它会削掉脂肪，把钱腾给更好的投资。

独立开发者常年面对的「成本慢慢爬上去，你却没感觉」，终于有了一个很具体的对手方。不是再订一份监控 SaaS，是直接让模型读你的账单。

原文

Biz expenses down to ~$300/mo

💸 Update: My total biz expenses have now dropped to just ~$300/mo!

This is to run all my websites/apps serving per year:

  • 20,000 paying customers
  • 252 million visitors
  • 2.4 billion requests
  • 2.4 petabyte (PB) in bandwidth

(~$8,000/mo if you add the $7,000/mo GPU bill and $800/mo R2 storage I pay for Photo AI, I exclude it above because it's one project that's so much more expensive in size than all the other sites together, but included in the chart below)

Claude Code helped me to find smart ways to save more money, AI is just really really really good at finding cost savings by itself, which is not so great for the economy short-term, but long term it trims all the fat and opens up spending for better investments I think

Anyway here's what it saved me in money, almost $34,000/mo:

  • $29,000/mo - switched to better and cheaper video models on Photo AI, video was very expensive and since I didn't update it ever it stayed expensive, also routed some image jobs to Google Cloud where I have some Google Cloud Credits, and also routed some jobs to Sume which sells AI models at market cost, very cool! This made my GPU bill go from $36,000/mo to $7,000/mo
  • $3,000/mo - consolidated my servers, cancelled Digital Ocean and Linode and moved everything to Hetzner saving about $3,000/mo
  • $1100/mo - analyzed my Backblaze B2 server backups, I had infinite versioning and lifecycle policies, that's reduced now to 30 days, this literally pushed the bill from $1,200/mo to $26/mo, about 50x cheaper! I had essentially versions of files for all my servers for over a decade, crazy!
  • $400/mo - similarly added Lifecycle Policies to my Cloudflare R2 bucket for Photo AI, pics are automatically put in cheaper Infrequent Access after 90 days, there was years of photos in there so this reduced the R2 bill from $1,200/mo to $800/mo
  • $118/mo - Claude analyzed all my Cloudflare Domain registrations, lots of domains I didn't use and didn't make sense to keep paying for, lots of things that also don't really make sense anymore in a post-AGI world, renewals for .io TLD are now $50/year which adds up fast!
  • $100/mo - Claude also analyzed my Claude subscription (yes!) and discovered I don't even use the Max 20x plan limits, so I downgraded from $200/mo to $100/mo

Even including Photo AI, I have now cut my costs by 90% from last year, getting me close to my biz expenses amount from a decade ago when I started building things

Costs slowly creep up over the years and you don't realize all the things you're spending on but AI is nice to help you figure all that out (also in your personal life!)

item.title: Amjad：员工电脑上的 AI Agent，正在变成企业系统风险
item.author: Amjad Masad
item.description:
有人靠禁 Claude Code 止血。Replit 的建议更硬：托管、隔离、凭证外置，让云端受管环境成为默认。

乔木改写

Amjad Masad 发了一份安全咨询，标题几乎不绕弯：

让受管云环境，成为 AI Agent 的默认运行方式。

背景是这几个月一串真实事件叠在一起：个人 Claude 账号被接到敏感防务环境的报道、Cursor 市场上被篡改的 Claude Code 扩展、Nx 供应链攻击里恶意包征用已装好的 AI CLI 去翻密钥、GitHub MCP 演示里一条恶意 Issue 就能诱导 Agent 把私有仓信息写进公开 PR……路径不同，失败模式很像：不可信内容被当成指令，执行环境权限过大，控制面还在 Agent 自己手里。

企业侧已经开始反应。有的直接限制 Claude Code 一类工具，高盛据称就是这么做的。Amjad 的判断是，禁用不解决长期问题。更干净的路是：

Agent 应该跑在组织可控、任务级隔离的环境里，只拿完成任务所需的最小资源。

咨询里列的控制项很工程化：验证过的执行隔离、经纪式凭证（credential broker）、逐步提权审批、任务作用域权限、网络与数据流限制、生产写入外置、供应链治理、以及 Agent 改不了的独立审计与熔断。

一句话概括他的立场：云托管本身不等于安全，但「受管云 + 可验证边界」比「员工笔记本 + 个人 Agent」更适合当默认值。

如果你正在给公司推 Coding Agent，这篇值得转给安全同事。争论焦点已经从「要不要用」换成「默认跑在谁的环境里」。

原文

Security advisory: Make managed cloud environments the default for AI agents

AI agents running on employee endpoints are becoming a systemic security risk for enterprises & governments.

Some are responding by restricting tools like Claude Code, as Goldman Sachs reportedly has.

In this security advisory, we outline the risks and recommend a path forward.

Security advisory: Make managed cloud environments the default for AI agents

AI agents should operate in dedicated, organization-controlled environments with limited access to the resources each task requires. Recent security incidents [5], [6] and research demonstrate why this is a growing necessity. Supply-chain attacks have always been able to compromise developer machines and recruit installed AI tools to search for sensitive corporate information and data. Agent harnesses are typically given broad privileges and have a shrinking amount of human oversight. Combined, these two effects are making agents an increasingly interesting target for attackers. Even unattended automations are being targeted: instructions hidden in a GitHub issue or email can redirect an agent toward private data and unauthorized actions. The rise of personal agents increases the risk even more, since they are insufficiently managed by organizations, mostly controlled by individuals, run with an inconsistent set of guardrails, and are incentivized to be proactive above all else: they read every email, every calendar invite; Every interaction is an opportunity to get prompt-injected. There is a better way forward: Organizations can continue adopting agents by giving them execution environments designed for software that reads untrusted content, runs code, and acts on a user’s behalf. In a world where agents are becoming more prevalent, @Replit believes that organizations must make managed, isolated cloud agents the default for autonomous development, with credentials, permissions, network access, and production changes controlled outside the agent’s reach. Adoption is growing faster than control AI development tools are becoming standard. Stack Overflow reports that the share of respondents using or planning to use AI tools rose from 70% in 2023 to 76% in 2024 [1] and 84% in 2025 [2]. This establishes the scale of AI-tool adoption and intent across annual respondent samples. Autonomous-agent usage falls outside the specific scope of this measure. Agent infrastructure is also expanding. Salt Labs [3] detected MCP-related infrastructure in 16.7% of its customer environments in January 2026 and 21.6% in August: a 4.9-percentage-point increase. These observations are limited to the vendor’s customer environments. Their applicability to the wider industry and the consistency of the customer cohort remain unestablished. The more consequential finding is the gap between deployment and control. In Salt Security’s October 2026 survey [3], 86.4% of respondents reported at least one agent operating in their organization, but only 17.5% could automatically stop an agent behaving unexpectedly in production. Only 12.5% could consistently trace complete agent paths across all agents.

乔木改写

Amjad Masad 发了一份安全咨询，标题几乎不绕弯：

让受管云环境，成为 AI Agent 的默认运行方式。

背景是这几个月一串真实事件叠在一起：个人 Claude 账号被接到敏感防务环境的报道、Cursor 市场上被篡改的 Claude Code 扩展、Nx 供应链攻击里恶意包征用已装好的 AI CLI 去翻密钥、GitHub MCP 演示里一条恶意 Issue 就能诱导 Agent 把私有仓信息写进公开 PR……路径不同，失败模式很像：不可信内容被当成指令，执行环境权限过大，控制面还在 Agent 自己手里。

企业侧已经开始反应。有的直接限制 Claude Code 一类工具，高盛据称就是这么做的。Amjad 的判断是，禁用不解决长期问题。更干净的路是：

Agent 应该跑在组织可控、任务级隔离的环境里，只拿完成任务所需的最小资源。

咨询里列的控制项很工程化：验证过的执行隔离、经纪式凭证（credential broker）、逐步提权审批、任务作用域权限、网络与数据流限制、生产写入外置、供应链治理、以及 Agent 改不了的独立审计与熔断。

一句话概括他的立场：云托管本身不等于安全，但「受管云 + 可验证边界」比「员工笔记本 + 个人 Agent」更适合当默认值。

如果你正在给公司推 Coding Agent，这篇值得转给安全同事。争论焦点已经从「要不要用」换成「默认跑在谁的环境里」。

item.description:
没有开源引擎可借，从 x86 机器码翻到 C，再编成 WebAssembly。他说自己大多时候只是在旁边看。

乔木改写

Pieter Levels 把可能是他最爱的游戏，《Battlefield 1942》，搬进了浏览器，还带多人联机。

地址：bf1942.pieter.com（免费试玩版）。

这事比他以前移植 Quake、DOOM 难一截。后两者早有开源项目垫底；BF1942 几乎没有任何现成底座，厂商也没开源引擎。半年前他试过，基本放弃。今天又拿 Opus 5.5 问了一句：「能不能把这个文件夹里的 BF1942 demo 移植到网页」。

然后他和 Claude Code（他承认主要是 Claude）干了一堆听起来离谱的事：

  • 反汇编 x86，找出约 57,000 个函数
  • 把每个函数翻成 C（mov eax, [esi+0x110] 变成 eax = READ32(esi + 0x110)）
  • 吐出大约 10 万行 C
  • 用 Emscripten 编成 WebAssembly
  • 重写约 300 个 Windows / Direct3D 调用，接到 WebGL 2 / OpenGL
  • 自建网络栈，经 WebSocket 连多人服务器

他自己的原话很诚实：「我不知道它怎么做到的，但它做到了，而且好像能玩。」

这不是怀旧彩蛋那么简单。它在演示一件更锋利的事：当模型能在「无文档、无开源、只有二进制」的场景里硬凿出可运行系统，软件考古和废弃游戏保存，会突然变得可规模化。

原文

Battlefield 1942 decompiled to the browser

I decompiled probably my favorite game ever: Battlefield 1942 and I put it on the web with multiplayer for you to play here:

👉 https://t.co/6C8H8KtSaU 👈

(It's the free shareware demo)

It was way harder than the other ports like Quake and DOOM I did because they already had lots of open source projects and work behind them

In case of Battlefield 1942 there was literally absolutely nothing to work on top of, nobody had ever ported it and there was no open source engine for it, nor did the makers ever open source it (like id Software did with Quake 3)

I tried it 6 months ago and essentiay gave up but I tried it today again with Opus 5.5 asking "can you try port the BF1942 demo in this folder to web"

So me and Claude Code (well let's be honest mostly Claude Code) did crazy shit today:

  • it disassembled the x86 raw machine code to find 57,000 x86 functions

item.title: Karpathy 周末两小时：用 Claude 从 4300 万条 HN 评论里筛出 6454 个值得看的视频
item.author: Andrej Karpathy
item.description:
受够了 YouTube 推荐，他把二十年 Hacker News 评论扔给 Opus 5.5，做了个不登录也好用的 HackerTube。

乔木改写

Andrej Karpathy 又交了一份周末作业。

这次叫 HackerTube。起因很简单：他烦 YouTube 推荐。于是让 Claude 把 Hacker News 二十年、大约 4300 万条评论滤了一遍，留下会反复被推荐的 6454 个视频。他自己说，用 Opus 5.5 大概花了两小时，观感「显著更好」。

站点在 hackertube.org。几个设计选择挺对味：

  • 不登录也能用，状态留在浏览器本地
  • 缩略图取视频中间的一帧，不跟那种被 A/B 测到极致的封面卷
  • 评论分析的底层数据打包成 zip，你也可以丢给 Claude，做自己的版本
  • 还有 HackerTube Longs

过程也值得记一笔。他默认用 Claude Code 桌面端、Opus 5.5 Medium。自己动手的部分很少：去 Google Cloud 开 YouTube API key、起一台 VPS、买域名。机器起来之后，把 IP 丢给 Claude，让它更新、加固、部署、优化，整条链路基本交给模型。

他收尾那句很轻，但分量不轻：

很多原本要花几周甚至几个月的项目，现在早饭前就能 few-shot 出来。我们还没想到的，还有多少？

这不是又一个「AI 写了个玩具」的故事。它更像在提醒：当你真正把「找信号」这件事外包给模型，产品形态会跟着变。HN 评论里本来就埋着高质量推荐，只是以前没人愿意花两小时把矿挖干净。

原文

Weekend hack: HackerTube

Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. Significantly better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5: https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

  • Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
  • Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
  • Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
  • HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process: I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.
